# {{< meta event.title >}} {.unnumbered .unlisted}

**Create research that others can reproduce and build upon.** An open, hands-on course on computational reproducibility – from organizing your first project to publishing complete and executable research.
{{< event register >}}
[Set up your computer](pages/00-setup.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[Browse the lessons](contents.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
::::

:::: {.home-aside}
[What you will build]{.home-aside-label}

### A project that anyone can rerun

- **Organize** it, and keep the raw data untouched
- **Track** every change with Git version control
- **Lock** the software with Pixi, and ship it in containers
- **Report** results with Quarto and Jupyter
- **Automate** the pipeline with Snakemake and Nextflow
- **Share** it with an open license and a DOI via Zenodo

::: {.home-command}
[\$]{.home-prompt} `pixi run reproduce`
:::

[One command rebuilds every result, on a computer that has never seen the
project.]{.home-aside-note}

## Can you rerun it in five years?

Your analysis worked last month. Can you rerun it today? Can a reviewer, a
labmate, or you in five years? These lessons teach the tools and habits that
make the answer *yes*: project organization, data management, literate
programming with Quarto and Jupyter, version control with Git and GitHub,
software environments with Pixi, containers, workflow managers (Snakemake and
Nextflow), documentation, and open publication.

::: {.home-figure}
![](assets/images/social-preview.png){fig-alt="Diagram:"}
:::

## One project together, then your own

::::: {.home-cards .home-cards-2}
:::: {.home-card .home-project}
[Guided project]{.home-card-kicker}

### The LTEE project

All hands-on excercise are around one project of variant calling from Richard Lenski's [Long-Term Evolution
Experiment](pages/ltee-project.qmd). You do not need to know genomics: the analysis is a given
pipeline, and the lessons are about making it reproducible.

::: {.content-visible when-profile="course"}
[What to hand in](assessment/ltee-project.qmd){.home-card-link}
:::
::::
:::: {.home-card .home-capstone}
[Your own research]{.home-card-kicker}

### Your capstone

The capstone is your own existing or ongoing computational research project with a datasets, code and results. You apply to it what each lesson teaches.

[The capstone](assessment/capstone-rubric.qmd){.home-card-link}

## Built on open material

This course began as a [mini-course at Stanford Biosciences](https://explorecourses.stanford.edu/search?q=BIOS+259&view=catalog&page=0&filter-coursestatus-Active=on&collapse=&academicYear=20232024)
([BIOS259, Winter 2024](https://github.com/asntech/bios259-w24/)), developed by Aziz Khan and taught with the help of
Alvina, Clemens and Brennan.

The material adapts and extends open lessons from [NBIS](https://nbisweden.github.io/),
[Software Carpentry](https://software-carpentry.org), [Data Carpentry](https://datacarpentry.org/) and many more. See [Sources and credits](pages/credits.qmd).
::::
:::: {.home-footer-side}
